newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan February export orders down 1.7 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan February export orders down 1.7 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods fell 1.7 percent to US$8.697 billion in February compared to February 1996, the economics ministry said on Thursday.
The official February export order figure was somewhat below an average forecast of a 0.45 percent downturn that resulted from a March 18 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.

That survey had shown highly divergent expectations, ranging from a pessimistic forecast of a 3.92 percent downturn in February export orders to the most optimistic forecast of a 1.56 percent year-on-year rise.

The finance ministry's chief statistician, Chang Yao-chung, attributed the decline to fewer working days in February compared to February 1996 as well as to lower export prices.

Although Taiwan's main annual holiday, traditional Chinese lunar new year, fell in February in both years, there were only 17.5 working days in February 1997 compared to 19 in February 1996, which contributed to the downturn in orders, Chang said.

Chang said the volume of export orders in Taiwan's two leading export sectors, information technology and electronics, actually had risen in February compared to February 1996, but that a sharp 10 percent fall in average prices in those sectors contributed to a decline in the value of overall orders.
